title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. I is a 4-element set; in the moduli context it is probably the 4-element structure attached to a level-2 or level-4 datum, but that is not visible on this page. V = V_I is the Klein four-group of double transpositions. J ≅ P_{2,2}(I) is the 3-element set of partitions of I into two pairs; equivalently J is identified with V \ {1}. G = S_I ≅ S_4 ≅ Aut^+(Cube), the rotation group of the cube. In this model I is the set of 4 main diagonals of the cube and J is the set of 3 face axes (the 'directions of faces'). The previous page set up this cube as a combinatorial map ('carte orientée') built from Circ(I) → J and P_2(I) → J. The next page classifies the homogeneous spaces of G in cube language.

This page lists the dictionary between cube elements and group elements that remains to be made explicit.
(a) The 8 vertices correspond to the 8 elements of order 3. Each vertex gives the 2π/3 rotation about its main diagonal, oriented from that vertex: 'rotations-sommets'.
(b) The 6 pairs of antipodal edges correspond to the 6 transpositions ('réflexions' of S_I). Each edge pair gives the π-rotation about the axis through the two edge midpoints; this rotation acts on the 4 diagonals as a transposition.
(c) The 6 faces correspond to the 6 elements of order 4, i.e. the circular permutations of I. Each face gives the π/2 rotation about its axis, oriented by that face.

Requirement. All three correspondences need a canonical orientation of the cube. That is, the F_2-torsor ω of orientations must be described intrinsically in terms of I.

Computation.
- For i ∈ J, let Q_i be the order-4 square structure attached to i, i.e. the pair of faces orthogonal to axis i. Let ω_i be its 2-element set of orientations.
- Claim 1: the orientation torsor of the cube is ω ≅ ∧_{i∈J} ω_i. Here ∧ denotes the contracted product (sum) of F_2-torsors.
- Claim 2: ω_i ≅ ω ∧ D_i. Here D_i = I/i is the 2-element set of blocks of the partition i, read as the two diagonals/codiagonals of Q_i.
- Substituting, ∧_i ω_i ≅ ω^{∧3} ∧ (∧_i D_i) ≅ ω ∧ (∧_i D_i). Consistency therefore amounts to the formula ∧_{i∈J} D_i ≅ 1, the trivial F_2-torsor.
- Proof of the formula. The natural map I → ∏_{i∈J} D_i is injective, since three partitions separate points. The target is an F_2^J-torsor; I is a torsor under V.
- The double transposition σ_j fixes the blocks of j and swaps the blocks of each i ≠ j. Hence V embeds in F_2^J as V_J(F_2) = {x ∈ F_2^J : Σx_i = 0}.
- So I ↪ ∏D_i is a reduction of structure group to the kernel of the sum map. Pushing forward along Σ: F_2^J → F_2 therefore gives a trivial torsor, i.e. ∧D_i ≅ 1.
- The next page confirms: 'restriction du groupe structurel : V_J(F_2), d'où ∧ D_i ≃ 1, OK.'

Geometric meaning. ∏_{i∈J} D_i is the 8-element vertex set of the cube, written as {±1}^3 in intrinsic coordinates. The image of I is one of the two inscribed regular tetrahedra.

Modular role (the likely purpose). The cube, or its dual octahedron, is the regular map, in the sense of a dessin, of the level-4 modular curve: PSL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4. Its 6 faces/cusps, 8 vertices and 12 edges correspond to the order-4, order-3 and order-2 data. The page is making the level-structure ↔ cube dictionary canonical, including orientation.
errors: No mathematical error found. The torsor argument (reduction of structure group from F_2^J to the sum-zero subgroup V_J(F_2), hence ∧D_i trivial) is correct.
Notational slippage: the subscripts on ω (ω_J, ω_𝕀, ω_I) are inconsistent on the page. The identification ω_i ≅ ω ∧ D_i is asserted, not proved here.

ideas.what: Rotation group of cube ≅ S_4 acting on the 4 diagonals. Vertices ↔ order-3 elements, antipodal edge pairs ↔ transpositions, faces ↔ 4-cycles.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th c.; Klein, Lectures on the Icosahedron)
ideas.where_published: Cube/octahedron maps are alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme in the dessins context; this specific dictionary is not known in print by Grothendieck.

ideas.what: Canonical orientation of the cube from I via contracted products of F_2-torsors: ∧_{i∈J} D_i ≅ 1, proved by the reduction of structure group I ↪ ∏ D_i from F_2^J to V_J(F_2).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/gerbe bookkeeping; Klein group as the sum-zero subgroup of F_2^3

ideas.what: Vertex set of the cube as ∏_{i∈J} (I/i), with I embedded as an inscribed tetrahedron.
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic coordinates of the cube from a 4-set; two inscribed tetrahedra

ideas.what: Cube viewed as the oriented map attached to S_4 ≅ PSL_2(Z/4), i.e. level-4 structures on elliptic curves.
ideas.modern_name: Regular dessin of the modular curve X(4) (octahedron/cube)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein; later dessins literature (Grothendieck, Jones–Singerman, etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the classical S_4–cube dictionary plus a neat, correct torsor-theoretic way to make the cube's orientation canonical in terms of a 4-element set. It is characteristic of Grothendieck's 'canonical, choice-free' style, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'ens. des diag. pour la corr. [?] Q_i' and the following line read more like 'ens. des deux codiagonales de Q_i' / 'ens des diag. pour le carré Q_i, i.e. D_i = I/𝔅_i', with 'ens. translations induites par i' beneath.
The struck '6 orientations de Card(I)' is more likely '6 orientations de Circ(I)' or similar; the replacement is '6 faces du cube'.
Under ∧D_i ≃ 𝟙 the annotation is 'torseur sous F_2' (struck 'torseur J'); under I ↪ ∏D_i the annotations are 'torseur sous V_J(F_2)' and 'torseur sous F_2^J'.
Under ω_i ≃ ω ∧ D_i the left annotation reads approximately 'ens. des deux orient. de Q_i' / 'ens. des deux codiagonales de Q_i'.
In the first displayed formula the left side looks like ω_𝕀 (cube/structure symbol), defined as ω_𝕀 (≃ ω_I), rather than ω_J.
Archive page number 23 is at the bottom left; the next page carries Grothendieck's own numbering 12.
